pitfalls: Fact-check method note: WebFetch was blocked by the network egress proxy for every domain tried in this pass (candycrush.fandom, mariowiki, mini-metro.fandom, dinopoloclub, nintendowire, gamedeveloper, blog.builtbysnowman, sixcolors, killscreen, techpp, dots.helpshift, angrybirds.com). Checks therefore rest on WebSearch result snippets. The session's WebSearch budget (200) ran out after the Candy Crush (x2), Super Mario Run (x2), Mini Metro/Motorways, Where's My Water, Bad Piggies/Hitman GO and core Alto's Zen Mode findings were verified. Two Dots, Angry Birds 2, Monument Valley and the Alto's Odyssey-specific details were NOT re-verified and are marked low or medium accordingly.

Revoking prestige: Candy Crush took away all earned Master Trophies on 29 Sept 2021 (v212.02), and Master Titles were removed separately. Remix stars, gold frames and Passport titles should be permanent once earned, including across rebalances of the solver or generator. Version the Remix generator so old results stay valid.

Rule drift: Candy Crush's Sugar Star condition appears to have changed from '2x the three-star score' to 'finish with 5+ moves to spare', so the same badge means different things to different players. Do not redefine Remix star conditions after launch. If they must change, keep old awards under the rules they were earned with.

Unprovable mastery targets: Candy Crush's historical Sugar Star was a flat 2x the three-star score, and players started 'Impossible Sugar Stars?' threads. A flat multiplier on Pocket Planet's classic targets could produce Remix targets the greedy solver cannot prove reachable. Always take Remix targets from a solver run on the remixed seed itself.

'First try' mastery (Candy Crush Gold Crowns), first-attempt-only scoring (Mini Motorways Daily Challenges, where players complained that practice runs counted) and permanent-placement hard rules (Mini Metro Extreme, Mini Motorways Expert) punish experimenting and can frustrate young children. Remix should allow unlimited retries, keep the best result, and state its constraints before play.

Parallel-track maintenance: Candy Crush's hand-built Dreamworld stopped getting new episodes in May 2015 and was removed from mobile in Dec 2016 so King could focus on main-world levels, and players were upset. Remix must be generated, not hand-built, so it never competes with the main pipeline.

Repetition fatigue: a Super Mario Run blogger who called Remix 10 its 'purest form' later lost interest and framed that around its rewards. Remix needs a reward track with a clear end (gold frame plus Passport title), not an open-ended drip.

Streaks, expiring rewards and random loot (as reported for Angry Birds 2: a 7-day streak legendary chest and same-day-only cards; not re-verified in this pass) run on loss aversion and chance and break our kid-safe money rules. Never tie Remix rewards to streaks, dates or randomness.

Pay-to-skip: the original Angry Birds sold the Mighty Eagle as an in-app purchase that could clear an unbeaten level (on a cooldown), which made a paid item part of level mastery (not re-verified in this pass). Nothing that skips or eases Remix may ever be sold.

Paid 'more of the same' for a game players see as complete drew 1-star reviews (Monument Valley's $1.99 Forgotten Shores, which ustwo responded to publicly). Keeping Remix free with no new currency avoids this.

Time-limited events with a short window (Two Dots Treasure Hunts, reportedly 4 days; not re-verified) create FOMO. Because Pocket Planet's date-seeded content can be regenerated for any past date, missed dailies and weeklies can stay replayable forever, with no lives and no expiry.

Remix seeds that re-roll on every attempt (confirmed: Super Mario Run's Remix 10 picks random course snippets each run) make star-chasing feel random and unfair. Keep each chapter's Remix seed fixed so retries are deterministic, and let children replay the exact same remixed planet.

Diluting the classic progression: if Remix stars count toward the same totals as classic stars, the harder mode can feel mandatory. Keep separate counters, as Mini Metro keeps achievements out of Endless, and never gate campaign progress behind Remix.

Over-heavy completionism: Super Mario Run hides a single bonus course behind all 120 Black Coins. Keep Remix rewards chapter-sized (10 planets leading to one gold frame) so goals stay reachable for children.

Mechanic-copy check: the applyToRemix texts were reviewed so they borrow principles, not mechanics. There is no three-colour coin ladder, no random-snippet fail-forward run, no Moon Scale-style fail rule, and no streak or chest rewards. Every Remix reward stays fixed, previewable and cosmetic, with no new currency.

Difficulty walls from stacking penalties: Slay the Spire's 20 cumulative Ascension modifiers, and Shovel Knight NG+'s double damage, scarcer healing and two checkpoints per stage, show how stacked penalties become walls. Pocket Planet should apply one twist per remix planet, and every star target must be proven by the solver under that twist.

Completion-gate grind: Super Mario 3D World's World Crown needs every Green Star and Stamp plus every gold flag, and its Mystery House Marathon sends you back to challenge 1 after any failure. Don't gate the Passport title or the gold frame on 3-starring everything; use totals or 'finished Remix', and never make a failure erase progress on other planets.

Mastery gates on a fun variant can lock casual players out: Mario Kart 8 v4.1 (1 May 2015) made Mirror and 200cc available by default instead of gated behind 150cc golds, and a Tetris Effect update removed the 'clear Normal first' gate on Expert. Unlock Remix on chapter completion, not on perfection.

Time pressure for kids: Galaxy's Speedy comets and Rayman Legends' Invasion rockets at 40/50/60 s with one hit point and no checkpoints add stress. Keep Remix untimed beyond the normal level length and always show the star targets before the first throw.

Expiring or limited-try offers: Rhythm Heaven's Perfect Campaign gives three tries and then disappears or moves on. This creates fear of missing out and failure anxiety that doesn't suit kids, so Remix must never expire or cap attempts, and date-seeded daily content should not gate Remix rewards.

Randomized unlock presentation: Rayman Legends unlocks its Back to Origins levels through scratch-card 'Lucky Tickets' (match three images). Even with a free currency this is a gambling-style reveal, which our kid-safe money rules forbid. All Remix unlocks and rewards must be deterministic and shown in advance.
Harsh failure stakes: Hollow Knight's Steel Soul is permadeath. A failed Remix planet must never delete, lock or reset progress.

Prestige dilution: gold cosmetics (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's Gold Mario has the same stats as Metal Mario, and each gold part is tied to a specific feat) only mean something because they are earned. Selling Remix-only gold art in the iMessage sticker pack would empty the gold frame and title of meaning, and would blur the kid-safe line between earned and paid items.

Repetition fatigue: a remix that only raises numbers on an identical layout feels like a chore. The classics always add a perceptible change (a named twist, a mirrored layout, a night palette, an invading cast, guest-remixed music), so each remix planet needs a change a player can see or hear, not only harder targets.

Carried-over power trivializes or confuses: Shovel Knight NG+ keeps upgrades and relics, and several feats (Hurry Up, Penny Pincher, Beeline and others) become impossible there. Remix should carry no power over, and should say clearly which badges can be earned there.

Cloning risk in the twist deck: several twist ideas map closely onto a named mode in another game (mirror track, timed comet, timed invasion). Keep the methodology (one visible change to a known layout) but build every twist from Pocket Planet's own parameters (spin, gravity strength, tray contents, starting land, creature goals), with its own names, and have the solver check it.

Research caveat (not a design pitfall): in this fact-check pass WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy for every domain tried (celeste.ink, mariowiki.com, mario.fandom.com, slaythespire.wiki.gg, theportalwiki.com, nintendolife.com, en.wikipedia.org, hollowknight.wiki, thegamer.com), and the session's WebSearch budget ran out near the end. Every claim above was checked against WebSearch result snippets for the cited pages, not the full pages. Corrections made: the NES Remix 501/504 star thresholds are from NES Remix 2; the Mario Kart 8 Deluxe gold-part unlocks were fixed; the Portal Advanced 13 example was fixed; the Hollow Knight early-unlock code is confirmed only for Silksong; the Galaxy 2 Speedy comets start with less time plus +10 s clocks; the Tetris Effect Expert gate was later removed. The Galaxy 2 Grandmaster Galaxy and DKC Tropical Freeze examples from the draft pitfalls were dropped because they could not be re-verified.

Grind gates: a prestige track earned by volume (wins or hours) instead of skill on a fixed set is understood and earned by very few players and trains grinding. Brawl Stars reportedly removed Masteries after only 11.8% of players ever earned a Title. Cap Remix at a fixed 10 planets / 30 stars per chapter.

Prestige that pays: attaching currency, power or items to mastery (Pokemon GO catch bonuses and Gym Badge items, Clash Royale mastery Gems) turns an optional badge into an obligation. Any random reward attached to prestige would also break the 'no random rewards' rule.

Per-attempt cost, pay-to-continue, or subscription-only mastery (Duolingo Legendary reportedly cost free users 100 gems per attempt, with a paid continue). Remix attempts must be free and unlimited, with no continue offer.
Decaying or redefined prestige: Duolingo skills 'cracked' over time, and Legendary changed meaning more than once. Earned Remix stars and gold frames must be permanent and survive retuning.
Scarcity windows: Rhythm Heaven's randomly chosen Perfect Campaign gives three attempts, then moves to another stage. Never rotate, expire or limit tries on Remix or Perfect stamps.

Permanent tarnish for struggling: NSMB Wii reportedly loses the save file's sparkle for good once the Super Guide merely appears, and NSMB U reportedly made it recoverable. Any 'unassisted' marker must be re-earnable, and Remix must never change base-chapter completion.

Shaming language: Celeste's Assist Mode text had to drop wording that called the default difficulty 'essential'. Remix failure and help copy must never suggest a child is playing wrong or is 'not good enough'; praise the shot or strategy, not talent.

Social comparison and engagement levers aimed at kids: Apple's HIG itself presents recurring leaderboards as a way to 'increase engagement'. Do not add a Remix leaderboard, and make sure everything works when parents restrict Game Center in Screen Time.

Commerce at the mastery moment: shop buttons or 'unlock more' prompts on Remix results or gold-frame celebrations break the spirit of Apple guideline 1.3. The iMessage sticker extension also needs no purchases and no link-outs outside a parental gate.
Lures at exit points, fake urgency and parasocial pressure (Radesky 2022): no Remix pop-up on pause, quit or session end; no countdowns; no sad or pleading creatures when Remix is declined.

FOMO and no natural stop (ICO Children's Code Standard 13 guidance and the 2023 games tips): no expiring remixes, no Remix streaks, no push notifications about Remix, no auto-starting the next remix. Save stars per planet so leaving loses nothing.

Hard difficulty walls (my own inference, not from a source): the greedy solver proves a score is reachable, not that a 6-year-old's shaky aim can reach it. Tougher Remix star targets should leave a clear gap below the solver's score, especially for 3 stars and on Hard, Super Hard and boss planets. Consider setting Remix 1-star at the base game's 2-star level.

Unclear always-on goals for pre-literate players (my inference, linked to Apple's voiceover suggestion for pre-literate kids): show Remix goals as icons with optional voiceover before the first throw, and keep one goal per planet.

Completion-percentage pressure (my inference): showing Remix % on every chapter card makes optional content feel required. Keep Remix progress to the completed chapter's card badge, the Remix view and the Passport.

Repetition fatigue (my inference): remixing the same chapter can feel samey. Make sure remix seeds actually change planet layout and gravity sources, and let players leave a Remix at any time with progress kept.
Locked stickers (my inference): gating iMessage stickers behind Remix progress would mean sharing game progress with the extension and would nag kids. Ship the pack fully unlocked and static.

Fact-check note: in this pass the web search budget was used up and the network proxy blocked every non-Apple domain (Supercell, fandom wikis, Bulbapedia, MarioWiki, Wikipedia, ICO, JAMA, PubMed, UNICEF, games press). Only Apple pages were opened and confirmed: App Review Guidelines 1.3 and 3.1.1, the Kids apps page, the Game Center HIG (via its JSON endpoint) and WWDC20 session 10145. The other findings rest on the original researcher's search excerpts, checked against general knowledge. Precise figures marked 'reportedly' or 'not re-opened' (11.8%, Clash Royale gem amounts, 45%/20%, 787 children in 18 countries, the Feb 2026 Brawl Stars change) should be checked before they are quoted publicly.

If the iMessage App Icon set is missing or incomplete, the extension can fail to show up ('unknown to FrontBoard') even though the build succeeds; Apple DTS's answer was to provide every icon (forum thread 797781). Any transparent pixel in those icons fails upload with ITMS-90647 (QA1686).

QA1686 and the current HIG list different iMessage icon sizes (iPad 134x100 vs 143x100; App Store 1024x768 vs 1024x1024). Fill whatever slots Xcode's iMessage App Icon set shows, and compose the art for the 4:3 shape.

The 500 KB limit covers the whole file, including every APNG frame. Xcode only warns, and an oversized animated sticker can fail to peel off or send blank at runtime. Enforce the limit in our export script or CI, and test the largest sticker sequence on a device, since how the limit applies to a compiled .stickersequence is unconfirmed.

stickerCanvas(id, px) is not an exact-pixel exporter: it multiplies by devicePixelRatio (capped at 2) and sets a CSS size. Export by drawing with drawSticker/drawCreature on a canvas of exactly 408 or 618 px, in headless Chromium like resources/render-art.cjs, because this art needs a browser Canvas 2D and the project has no node-canvas.
Mixing sticker sizes in one pack goes against the HIG. Pick Regular (408 px, 3 per row) or Large (618 px, 2 per row) and render everything at that size.

Capacitor SPM takes the CapApp-SPM platform from the FIRST IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in project.pbxproj. A new extension target that Xcode creates with a newer iOS default can bump Package.swift, or break it: at iOS 18 or higher with swift-tools 5.9 it cannot resolve. Pin the extension to 15.0 (not 17.0 as in the SnapWorth PR) and check Package.swift after every `cap sync`.

`npx cap add ios` rewrites every PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER to the appId (com.pocketplanet.game). Regenerating the ios folder would give the extension the app's own id, and the build or upload would then fail.

Guideline 4.4 bans marketing, advertising and in-app purchases inside extensions. No 'get more stickers' or 'play now' hooks, and no paid sticker sets; paid sets would also conflict with our kid-safe money rules.
Guideline 5.2.5 bans Apple emoji in sticker packs, and 4.5.6 bans embedding Apple emoji in the binary. Draw our own expressions.

A bundled extension inherits the game's category and cannot use the Stickers category, so it gets no sticker-store discovery of its own. Moving it to a standalone app later means creating a new app record.

A no-code pack is static and cannot read game progress. Exporting rarity-tiered or earned album stickers (drawSticker's RARITY_BG) would give everyone the rare ones and cheapen the in-game album. Keep a separate chat set.
Content cannot rotate: our date-seeded festivals cannot change a static pack. Festival stickers stay in the pack year-round or wait for app updates. Avoid stickers that only make sense on one date.

Localization is weak. accessibility-label is one string per sticker with no documented localization key, and the SnapWorth PR shipped English-only labels. Text baked into sticker images cannot be localized either, so keep stickers wordless and test VoiceOver in ja/fr/pt/de/es.

Apple's NSStickerSharingLevel paragraph prints the value as `{OS}` and ends with an unclear sentence ('If you add this key to your app, your sticker pack doesn't appear in the list'). Declaring both the messages and media contexts makes stickers present only in the media context. Test both keys on a device before shipping either.

iMessage screenshots were reported as required even for a bundled pack. They must show fictional accounts and no phone numbers (sticker-submissions page; Guideline 2.3.9). Keep 'For Kids' wording out of the metadata unless the app is in the Kids Category (Guideline 2.3.8).
